consumer_ordering.builder: Publish the record before request fields and before lock9 acquisition. Preserve default/7/8 selector mapping, packing byte equal-to-one and untouched fields. Call the existing owned acquire directly.
consumer_ordering.first_completion: Enter nested critical; require both subscribers; clear the first subscriber; leave with the saved critical state; invoke the saved callback. Nested completion sees the cleared slot.
consumer_ordering.develop_job4: Null plane returns 0 with no effects. Otherwise fill plane +0x20/+0x24 (only when zero)/+0x28/+0x2c/+0x30, then the develop record fields in source order with completion callback 0x00e8eb18, publish the frame task, call the owned builder, wait for current-task event 0x10 with an infinite deadline, call owned clear-record release and return 8 when record byte 0x36 is nonzero.
consumer_ordering.record_notification: Signal event 0x10 to the task stored at 0x015b0ccc.
consumer_ordering.clear_record_release: Clear the record descriptor, then call the owned release.
consumer_ordering.boundaries: Whole ordinary Playback requirements initialization, second completion, reset, restart, timer cancellation, prefix preservation, submit, finish and cancel/restore are owned, as are develop job4, its record notification and clear-record release. The develop framework caller 0x00e936a8 and the overlay47 clear-record caller 0x01238160 remain outside this unit.
consumer_ordering.lifetime: The develop record and static request are constructed before reserved lock9 is acquired. In all three images the builder's only caller is job4 0x00e8ffe0 and job4's only caller is 0x00e93700; no literal pointer names any of the five entries. Serialization of that one constructor path across tasks is not established. Job4's wait is satisfied by any current-task event 0x10 and does not bind the wake-up to this record's completion, so record/request and subscriber quiescence remain unestablished.
